Source Basis: Core + RadPrimer + STATdx synthesis. Core supplies the board-level external-hernia/SBO framework; RadPrimer provides the canonical abdominal-wall hernia backbone and captions; STATdx adds supplemental mimic/complication examples.

📚 Summary
  • Abdominal-wall hernias are defects through which fat, bowel, or other viscera may protrude; acute concern centers on obstruction, incarceration, strangulation, and ischemia.
  • CT is the most accurate modality in the source package and is preferred first-line for acute presentations or suspected bowel compromise.
  • Ultrasound is useful in nonurgent evaluation, especially for reducibility or transient defects with upright positioning or Valsalva.

🖼️ Key Imaging Findings
CT
  • Assess hernia contents, neck, bowel obstruction, bowel-wall compromise, and ischemia.
  • Inguinal hernias are classified by relationship to the inferior epigastric vessels: indirect lateral, direct medial.
  • Femoral hernias enter the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament and may compress the adjacent femoral vein.
  • Obturator hernia places bowel between the obturator and pectineus muscles.
  • Spigelian hernia occurs along the semilunar line/lateral rectus margin; ventral hernias include epigastric, hypogastric, incisional, and parastomal defects.
  • Lumbar hernias traverse posterior abdominal-wall muscle or thoracolumbar fascia and may contain retroperitoneal or intraperitoneal structures.
Ultrasound
  • Dynamic maneuvers can elicit a transient hernia and help assess reducibility.
  • A fatty spermatic-cord liposarcoma mimic may be very echogenic.
MR Imaging
  • A spermatic-cord liposarcoma mimic may appear as a mass with fat signal extending through the inguinal canal.

⚖️ Differential Diagnosis
  • True hernias may be mimicked by hematoma, abscess, lymphadenopathy, soft-tissue neoplasm, hydrocele/varicocele, cryptorchidism, and spermatic-cord lipoma/liposarcoma.
  • Enterocutaneous fistula can mimic a hernia when gas or enteric contrast tracks into the abdominal wall; identify the tract rather than a true hernia sac.

⚠️ Pearls / Pitfalls
  • Incarceration means nonreducibility; strangulation means vascular compromise/ischemia.
  • Richter hernia involves only part of the bowel circumference, typically the antimesenteric wall, so obstruction may be absent despite strangulation risk.
  • Femoral, obturator, and spigelian hernias carry relatively high incarceration/strangulation risk in the source package.

  • Direct inguinal: medial to inferior epigastric vessels; indirect inguinal: lateral to them and may travel with the spermatic cord.
  • Femoral: below the inguinal ligament, in the femoral canal, with characteristic femoral-vein compression.

Localize the defect by fixed anatomic landmarks, then assess contents and complications; use dynamic US for reducibility when nonurgent and CT for acute or complicated presentations.

Imaging pivot: do not use absence of obstruction to exclude a dangerous Richter hernia.

column15: How do epigastric, hypogastric, incisional, and parastomal hernias fit under ventral hernia?

column15: What are the key localization and risk clues for lumbar hernia?

column11: What is the key diagnostic pitfall of Richter hernia?
column12:
Do not exclude dangerous hernia because there is no obstruction. Only the antimesenteric bowel wall is trapped, so the lumen may remain open while the wall segment becomes ischemic/strangulated.

column13: What should be distinguished when an abdominal-wall mass appears near a stoma or repair site?
column14:
Trap: assuming any stoma-adjacent or repair-site lump is recurrent/incisional hernia. Safety check: identify a true fascial defect and hernia sac. Abscess is a loculated subcutaneous fluid collection; metastasis can appear as a partly calcified abdominal-wall mass near a colostomy.

column15: How can spermatic-cord lipoma/liposarcoma mimic inguinal hernia, and what favors tumor?

A fat-containing spermatic-cord mass may extend through the inguinal canal into the scrotum and mimic a hernia. Tumor is favored when the lesion is expansile/mass-like, internally complex or has a soft-tissue component; the package example was fat signal on MRI and very echogenic on ultrasound.

column15: Define interparietal/interstitial hernia.
column16:
The hernia sac lies in fascial planes between abdominal-wall muscles without entering the subcutaneous soft tissues. Exam pivot: the sac is still within wall layers rather than protruding into subcutaneous fat.
